detail.longDescription: I would like to create a Lookup plugin that queries the inventory to gather some data on hosts and format them. I tried a jinja expression but I found the solution was convoluted and a pain to put together. Python code offers much more leeway to achieve that and plugin can be fast to code. So far, I came up with the following code but I don't know how to access the inventory I tried through the variables dict but apparently it is fed only contextually and variables.hostvars can end up being None class LookupModule(LookupBase): def run( self, terms: list[Any], variables: dict[str, Any] | None = None, **kwargs: Any, ) -> list[dict[str, str]]: self.set_options( var_options=variables, direct=kwargs) if variables is None: raise AnsibleError( "The Ansible variable context is unavailable") groups = variables.get("groups") hostvars = variables.get("hostvars") if groups is None: raise AnsibleError( "The Ansible variable 'groups' is None") if hostvars is None: raise AnsibleError( "The Ansible variable 'hostvars' is None") ... Here is the playbook I used to do some testing - name: Gather facts on reachable machines hosts: all gather_facts: yes tasks: - ansible.builtin.debug: msg: "Gathering facts" - name: Debug hosts: localhost gather_facts: yes tasks: - name: debug lb backends run_once: true vars: lb_backends_443: "{{ query( 'lde_lb_backends', group='rc1_lb_443', ipv4_only=true) }}" ansible.builtin.debug: var: "{{ avar }}" loop: - lb_backends_443 loop_control: loop_var: avar So how do you access the whole inventory from a plugin, here a lookup plugin because it seemed appropriate ?
